sents.t: In October, I found a scary envelope in my mailbox.
It was from the IRS, the government office that collects taxes.
My hands were shaking when I opened it.
The letter said that there was a problem with my tax return from last year.
It said that I hadn’t reported all of my income and that I owed four hundred dollars.
I called Danny immediately.
He told me not to panic.
He said that letters like this were common and that we would figure it out together.
That evening, he came over with his laptop.
We looked at my forms, and Danny asked me if I had worked anywhere else last year.
Then I remembered: last summer, I had done some translation work online for a small company.
They had sent me a tax form, but I hadn’t thought it was important.
“That’s it,” Danny said.
“The IRS knows about every payment.”
He explained that I needed to file a corrected return and pay the difference.
He said that if I paid quickly, the penalty would be small.
I paid the next day.
A month later, another letter arrived.
It said that everything was now correct.
Danny told me to keep all my tax papers in one folder.
I’ve already bought one.
It’s bright red, so I can’t lose it.

comp.q: Why did Sam buy a bright red folder?
o: So he won’t lose his tax papers.
comp.fa: چرا سام یک پوشه‌ی قرمز روشن خرید؟
